title: What the edge of space did to his bare hand 🎈
subject: kittinger
description:
Would you have stepped off that ledge? 👇

In 1960, Air Force Captain Joe Kittinger rode a balloon to 102,800 feet. On the way up, the pressure glove on his right hand failed, and the near-vacuum made his hand swell to twice its size.

Sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, "Space Jumper" (Air & Space Quarterly, 2023) and "The Long, Lonely Leap" (2010); Holloman Air Force Base, "Anniversary of a record jump".
tags: what happens to your body at the edge of space

scenes.text: Your bare hand would swell to twice its size.
August 16, 1960. Air Force Captain Joe Kittinger rode a balloon to 102,800 feet.
On the climb, his right pressure glove failed. Up there, air pressure is about 1 percent of yours.
His hand puffed up, swollen and painful.
He jumped anyway, falling over 4 and a half minutes under what he called the blackest black he'd ever seen.
Back on the ground, his hand fully recovered.
